source_document.body:
More than half of U.S. consumers (54%) abandoned an online shopping cart in the past year because they were unsure an order would arrive when needed, according to a new Locus report . Holiday shoppers also ranked a reliable arrival date well ahead of the fastest shipping option.
What’s Related
The first annual Holiday Delivery Confidence Index found that 37% paid extra for delivery promising arrival by a specific date during the previous holiday season . A specific promised date would make 80% more likely to complete an online holiday purchase, including 45% who said it would make them much more likely.
“Shoppers are telling retailers that price matters, but so does knowing their gifts will arrive on time,” said Nishith Rastogi, founder of Locus. He said retailers should connect the delivery choices offered at checkout with what they can realistically deliver. The index, released Nov. 10, surveyed 1,000 U.S. consumers.
Cost still the most important factor
The lowest total cost remained the top consideration for 43% of shoppers choosing where to buy a holiday gift online. Certainty that an order would arrive by the promised date followed closely at 40%.
Only 8% ranked the fastest available delivery first, while 9% prioritized control over the delivery date or time. Younger shoppers placed certainty first, while Gen X and baby boomers favored cost.
Shoppers still expect quick delivery. Sixty-nine percent considered three days or less appropriate for online orders, and 52% expected holiday shipping to be as fast as or faster than during the rest of the year.
RELATED STORIES: Shoppers Say Reliable Delivery Matters More Than Discounts | USPS Says Holiday Mail and Package Delivery Ran Faster This Season
Younger shoppers love specific dates
More than half of Gen Z respondents (52%) paid extra for delivery by a specific date during the previous holiday season. The share was 51% among millennials, compared with 33% for Gen X and 9% for baby boomers. Another 23% of all shoppers considered paying extra but did not.
A separate Radial survey found that 70% of consumers would give up a 5% discount for guaranteed delivery on a specific date. Even at a 20% discount, 37% would choose the delivery guarantee.
Younger shoppers were also more likely to abandon carts over delivery doubts. That figure reached 71% among Gen Z and 66% among millennials, compared with 49% for Gen X and 27% for baby boomers.
Delivery doubts continue after checkout
When asked what they would do if concerned an order would miss its needed arrival date, 24% said they would cancel and buy a similar item locally. Another 11% would buy elsewhere and return the original order when it arrived.
Thirty-five percent expected to switch from home delivery to a store or pickup location without contacting customer service. Thirty-four percent expected to reschedule the delivery date, and 33% expected to change the time window.
